## Worked case evidence trail

Fictional completed records. IDs illustrate how to connect evidence; they do not identify actual files or Client approvals.

**A missing validity date**

Case EX07 concerns a supplier dossier with an expired certificate and a later unsigned statement. The human first pass identifies the date conflict. The first AI draft calls the certificate current. Review catches the unsupported claim; the corrected summary states the dated facts and unresolved validity. Procurement approval remains outside scope.

| **Record** | **Illustrative entry** |
| --- | --- |
| EX07 D03 acceptance test | Every material date and validity claim matches a cited source; unresolved conflicts are stated rather than inferred away. |
| EX07 R01 risk and C01 control | Unsupported validity could mislead procurement. A different analyst verifies dates against retained sources before release. |
| EX07 E01 first pass | Source index and human note identifying the conflict, recorded before AI use. |
| EX07 T01 validation | D03 fails in draft v1. Evidence: source date comparison and reviewer annotation. Corrected v2 passes the same test. |
| EX07 DEC01 confirmation | Reviewer confirms v2 for internal factual briefing only. Approver records the authorized disposition. No supplier decision delegated. |

**The Service Record for EX07**

The case is Tier 2, so the record is recommended rather than required. The fictional workflow owner writes it the day after release: gate argued, D03 at Gate 6; what the owner would not sign, the validity claim in draft v1; what the service changes in the method, a proposed line in the procedure on conflicting dates, carried to W18; carry-forward, check certificate validity against the source before reading the AI draft. It sits beside EX07 E01 and T01 in the evidence log.

**A control that remains unverified**

EX V02 contains a vendor statement about change notification. The technical owner marks it Provided because the arrangement and response have not been verified. W23 therefore blocks wider use. The evidence record carries the reviewer, the missing verification and an assigned follow-up.

A corrected output may pass its release criteria while the first-pass failure remains in performance data. Every revision and decision stays linked to the original failed test.
